public_rationale: SiliconANGLE reported on May 20, 2024 that Murati denied Sky was designed to sound like Johansson, in a briefing with The Verge (e1). For that denial to be a lie, Sky would have to have been meant to sound like Johansson, and Murati would have to have known it. The evidence in this case shows neither. The Washington Post reported on May 22, 2024 that the actor's agent said neither Johansson nor the film 'Her' was ever mentioned by OpenAI. The Post also said the actor's natural voice sounds identical to Sky in voice-test recordings it reviewed (e2). That points toward the denial being accurate. But the agent spoke anonymously. NPR reported on May 31, 2024 that it was still unknown whether Altman privately told the casting team to use Johansson as an inspiration (e4). Murati was the sole decision-maker on the voices project, according to OpenAI's Joanne Jang (e3). Murati told NPR she did not know what Johansson sounded like until people began comparing Sky to her (e4). That is her own account. The evidence leans against the claim but does not settle whether Murati lied.
limitations: Murati's knowledge and state of mind cannot be observed directly. Most of the evidence on them comes from OpenAI or from people connected to the casting.
The original Verge interview was not retrieved. Murati's wording comes from secondary reports.
The case contains no casting direction notes, internal messages or testimony about what Murati knew.
